codeReview.summary: Clean, correct implementation of heuristic keyword routing with comprehensive test coverage. The _heuristic_route() function uses re.search with \b word boundaries for case-insensitive keyword matching, with coding keywords checked before research keywords to enforce priority. The route_and_run() function correctly chains: force_agent → auto_route=False → heuristic → LLM fallback → preferred. 38 well-structured tests across 13 classes cover all 16 VAL-RTR assertions. tests/test_agents.py was verified unmodified (empty git diff). Ruff passes clean. All 47 tests (38 router + 9 agents) pass.

issues.description: Tests reference ALL_AGENTS by index (ALL_AGENTS[0] for claude, ALL_AGENTS[2] for gemini) when patching .run(). If ALL_AGENTS ordering changes, tests silently break. Consider using a named lookup like next(a for a in ALL_AGENTS if a.name == 'claude') for resilience.

Regex patterns are compiled on each _heuristic_route() call (8 re.search calls worst-case). For a CLI tool this is negligible, but pre-compiling patterns at module level would be marginally more efficient.

test_heuristic_only_routes_if_agent_available tests the case where coding agents are unavailable but a coding keyword matches. A symmetric test for research keyword with no research agent available would complete the coverage, though not strictly required by the validation contract.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Worker moved 'from vox.engine import query_llm' from an inline import inside _pick_agent() to a module-level import. This changes the import topology — router.py now unconditionally imports engine.py at module load time. The AGENTS.md documents 'Use unittest.mock.patch for mocking external dependencies' but doesn't specify whether imports should be module-level or deferred. The change was necessary for test mockability (patch target must be where the name is looked up), so this is reasonable.
